page_text_ocr_zh:
出版者的话

古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：“任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。

现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。

情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期。一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心发展影响很长远。

当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。

这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。

让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧！
page_text_en:
Publisher's Note

The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry; that's not difficult. But to get angry at the right time, in the right place, in the right way, and with the right person, that's truly difficult.' What we now call emotional management refers precisely to expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time and place, and toward the right person.

In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills. Those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this ability, though perhaps intelligent, often struggle in their endeavors.

While emotional management skills may partly stem from innate factors, they ultimately rely on learning and cultivation through experience. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this period create permanent neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.

Currently, reading emotional management picture books together with children is a widely recognized method for cultivating these skills. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried into children's ears by parents' voices, taking root in their hearts, and growing with sunlight and rain.

This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks addresses specific emotional topics for children, illustrating their emotional journeys and how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a valuable reference for parents during shared reading.

Let us enjoy a wonderful journey of parent-child reading together with this series!
summary_zh: 本页为《小奶牛的烦恼》系列绘本的出版者序言，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的黄金期，并介绍了该系列绘本通过亲子共读帮助孩子认识和管理情绪的教育理念。

page_text_ocr_zh:
老师对你说
原来，我是最美的
一只叫艾美达的小奶牛平静地生活在一个美丽的农场里，她白色的皮肤上布满了黑色的斑点，产的奶特别香。这样一只可爱的小奶牛，大家都很喜欢。可是，小奶牛自己不这么认为，这只诺曼底小奶牛有个烦恼：她不喜欢自己身上的黑色斑点。她对着好朋友小老鼠诺米叹气，她羡慕隔壁农场的利木赞牛美露西，她像猪一样在泥潭里打滚儿，还让艺术家小猫芭莎在她身上画些美丽的图案。可是，这些举动让农场里的小动物们觉得太荒唐了，大家都觉得小奶牛拥有黑白相间的皮肤多幸运啊！
你猜，艾美达最后改变自己的样子了吗？家长们读到这里，可以问问怀里的宝贝：你觉得艾美达应该改变自己的样子吗？为什么？如果你是艾美达，你会怎么做？
后来，美露西拿出一本大大的书给艾美达看，书里有各种黑白相间的奇妙动物，艾美达被迷住了。原来，世界上还有这么神奇的事情；原来，自己的斑点真的很美！故事的结尾这样写道：“从此以后，艾美达每天都笑嘻嘻的，再也不烦恼了。”读到这里，读者一颗悬着的心终于可以放下来了。艾美达接受了自己样子，她还是那个白色的皮肤上布满黑色斑点的可爱小奶牛。
page_text_en:
Teacher Says to You
Turns out, I'm the most beautiful
A little cow named Emelda lived peacefully on a beautiful farm. Her white skin was covered in black spots, and her milk was especially fragrant. Such a cute little cow was loved by everyone. However, the little cow didn't think so. This Normandy calf had a烦恼: she didn't like the black spots on her body. She sighed to her good friend, little mouse Nomi, and envied the Limousin cow, Melody, from the neighboring farm, who rolled around in the mud like a pig and even let the artist cat Basha paint beautiful patterns on her. However, these actions seemed too absurd to the other animals on the farm. Everyone thought how lucky the little cow was to have black-and-white skin!
Guess what? Did Emelda finally change her appearance? Parents reading this can ask their children: Do you think Emelda should change her appearance? Why? If you were Emelda, what would you do?
Later, Melody showed Emelda a big book filled with various black-and-white animals. Emelda was fascinated. It turned out there were such amazing things in the world; her own spots were actually beautiful! The story ends like this: "From then on, Emelda smiled every day and never worried again." Reading this, the reader's anxious heart could finally rest. Emelda accepted her appearance and remained the same adorable little cow with white skin covered in black spots.
summary_zh: 本页为绘本《小奶牛的烦恼》的导读或教师指导页，通过讲述小奶牛艾美达因不喜欢自己身上的黑色斑点而烦恼，最终在朋友帮助下接受并爱上自己独特外貌的故事，引导读者思考自我接纳与自信的主题。

page_text_ocr_zh:
每个人都是独特的“我”，要学会正确认识自己，肯定并喜欢自己。只有自我肯定，才能获得源源不断的精神养分。很多时候，孩子会觉得
自己没有别人好，觉得自己有些地方比不上别人，然后羡慕别人，希望
成为别人，甚至不自觉地去模仿，去跟随。久而久之，他们会逐渐失去
自我，变得没有个性。作为父母，应该像那只利木赞母牛一样去帮助孩
子正确认识自我：我是有存在价值的，没有必要羡慕他人，只要做好自
己就可以了。

《小奶牛的烦恼》是一本图文俱佳的儿童绘本，通过美丽的图画、生
动的文字，表达了一种非常重要的思维：我就是我，我是很棒的。细细
品读，还会发现一些有趣的地方，比如：小奶牛和小老鼠身形的对比，剧
烈的大小反差带给小朋友强烈的视觉冲击；还有，小奶牛的表情贯穿了
整个故事，从开始的皱着眉头到最后的眉开眼笑，形象地表现了艾美达
心情的变化。相信这些细节会吸引孩子们去主动观察、理解，从而获得
丰富的故事情验。

让我们现在就翻开这本书吧！

（石家庄市第二幼儿园 谷红岩）
page_text_en:
Everyone is a unique 'me'. We should learn to recognize ourselves correctly, affirm and like ourselves. Only with self-affirmation can we gain continuous spiritual nourishment. Often, children feel they are not as good as others, feel they are inferior in some ways, then envy others, hoping to become someone else, even unconsciously imitating and following. Over time, they gradually lose themselves and become unoriginal. As parents, we should help children recognize themselves correctly, just like that Limousin cow: I have value, there's no need to envy others, just do my best.

"The Little Cow's Worry" is a beautifully illustrated children's picture book. Through beautiful pictures and lively text, it expresses a very important mindset: I am me, and I am great. Carefully reading it, you'll discover some interesting details, such as the contrast between the little cow and the little mouse's body shapes—the dramatic size difference gives children a strong visual impact. Also, the little cow's expressions run through the entire story, from frowning at the beginning to beaming with joy at the end, vividly showing Amida's emotional changes. These details will attract children to actively observe and understand, thus gaining a rich story experience.

Let's open this book now!

(Shijiazhuang No. 2 Kindergarten, Gu Hongyan)

这天早上，像平常一样，小奶牛怯生生地走出奶牛场。
她遇到了好朋友小老鼠诺米。
“艾美达，你今天好吗？”小老鼠问她。
“唉，还不是和平时一样。我长了一身的黑斑，可我一点儿也不喜欢！美露西真幸运，她身上就没有斑点，她长得多漂亮啊！”小奶牛叹了口气说。
美露西是隔壁农场的利木赞牛。她的皮肤是漂亮的深棕色，而且没有斑点！
page_text_en:
This morning, as usual, the little cow timidly walked out of the cowshed.
She met her good friend, the little mouse Nomi.
"Aimida, are you okay today?" the little mouse asked her.
"Sigh, it's just like always. I have all these black spots, and I don't like them at all! Mélodie is so lucky, she doesn't have any spots, and she's so beautiful!" the little cow sighed.
Mélodie is a Limousin cow from the neighboring farm. Her skin is a beautiful dark brown, and she has no spots!
summary_zh: 小奶牛艾美达因身上的黑斑而烦恼，遇到好朋友小老鼠诺米时，向她倾诉了自己羡慕隔壁农场没有斑点的美露西的心情。

page_text_ocr_zh:
小老鼠诺米看到她的朋友不开心，自己也高兴不起来。她想尽办法，想让小奶牛改变想法。可是没有用，艾美达怎么也开心不起来。她慢慢地朝牧场走去。
现在，连诺米也开始难过了。
page_text_en:
Little mouse Nomi saw her friend was unhappy, and she couldn't be happy either. She tried her best to change the little cow's mind. But it didn't work; Amada couldn't be happy no matter what. She slowly walked toward the pasture.
Now, even Nomi began to feel sad.
summary_zh: 小老鼠诺米试图安慰因斑点而烦恼的小奶牛艾美达，但未能成功，自己也因朋友的不开心而感到难过。
画面中，一只身上有黑色斑点的小奶牛艾美达站在高高的草丛中，表情忧伤，身旁的小老鼠诺米抬头看着她，显得关切而难过。背景是绿色的草地和远处的围栏，草叶上带有花纹图案，营造出一种梦幻的氛围。右下角有二维码及宣传文字，左下角标有页码“4”。

艾美达浑身沾满了泥巴，回答道：
“我不喜欢我的黑斑，可我浑身上下
到处都是。美露西的皮肤就只有

page_text_en:
Suddenly, Amada started rolling in the mud. What a spectacular sight!
Little pig Edmund asked her, "Amada, what's wrong? Are you crazy?"
Amada, covered in mud, replied:
"I don't like my black spots, but they're all over me.
Lucy's skin is just one color—how beautiful!"
summary_zh: 小奶牛艾美达因讨厌自己身上的黑斑，开始在泥潭里打滚，小猪埃德蒙惊讶地询问她，艾美达解释说她羡慕隔壁农场没有斑点的美露西。
画面中，小奶牛艾美达正躺在泥潭里打滚，身上沾满了泥巴，表情开心，周围散落着写有“泥”字的圆形图案，背景是绿色的树木和草地，营造出一种欢乐的氛围。
画面中，小奶牛艾美达穿着一件粉色花裙子，身上沾满泥巴，正开心地和小猪埃德蒙、小老鼠诺米以及一只小白兔在干草堆上玩耍。背景是晾晒着各色衣物的绳子，两只小鸟在绳子上嬉戏，营造出欢乐的农场氛围。

全
是泥！
“我们猪才在泥潭里打滚儿呢，你可是奶牛啊！”小猪埃德蒙提醒她。
“你现在看上去和美露西一样，皮肤是棕色的……但是泥巴滴得到处都是，多恶心啊！”小兔子奥古斯丁插嘴说。
“你的奶头上全是泥巴，牛奶会变成什么味儿啊？”小绵羊让诺补充道。
艾美达只好又一次难过地走开了。
page_text_en:
All
is mud!
"We pigs are the ones who roll in mud, you're a cow!" reminded Pig Edmund.
"You look just like Lucy now, with brown skin... but the mud is dripping everywhere, how disgusting!" interjected Rabbit Augustin.
"Your udders are full of mud, what will the milk taste like?" added Sheep Leno.
Amada had to walk away, sad once again.

page_text_en: On the way, Amada met the little cat Basha. Basha was an artist who spent all day daydreaming. But once he picked up his paintbrush, he could always paint wonderful pictures. All the little animals on the farm knew him.

"Basha, can you help me out?" she asked, "I want you to make me beautiful. Can you paint some beautiful patterns on me? Please, please!"
Basha thought this idea was brilliant. He took out his paintbrush.

page_text_en:
"Amada, your spots are beautiful, you don't need any other decorations!" Piglet Edmund insisted.
"But I'm black and white, with no color at all, it's too plain!" Amada retorted.
Lamb Leno and rabbit Augustin tried to reason with her:
"If that's the case, we have reasons to complain too! Look! I'm pure black!" Leno said.
"And I'm pure white!" Augustin said.
Then, they said in unison:
"You're black and white, how lucky you are!"
